debunked.reason: Each test has exactly two simple scenarios; go.md RULE-GOLANG-TEST-007 (L956) and baseline (L856) prefer plain asserts for one or two simple cases; TEST-014 is a prohibition on tables, not an override of that carve-out.
Premise false: sessions.go:168/172 and proposals.go:181/186 also call s.presentation.language() per use, so repeated accessor reads are the in-repo pattern, not duplicated code.

The sweep only rewords file paths, rule/FACT/ACDSL IDs and schema/taxonomy jargon; a permission allowlist rule string is none of those, and smine-permissions L33 pins the rule string in change on casual installs.

Writing to bin/ to swap a verifier also lets the attacker swap bin/acdsl, which runs CheckPolicy; binaries are outside the policy by design, so a digest check by that binary closes nothing. Verifier bindings are already gated.

escalations.why: Persisted data: internal/sessions/sessions.go:223 validateScopeName admits '.. ' and '...'; on Windows trailing spaces/dots are stripped during path normalization, so DeleteScope('.. ') could RemoveAll the whole sessions directory. Undemonstrated: needs a Windows probe and confirmation that the unauthenticated loopback DELETE handler in internal/server passes the raw segment through.

Persisted config / command execution: install.env is sourced as shell code by install.sh and sync_settings.sh; if the Go configserver -install writer (writeInstallEnv) or any HTTP-reachable path writes PEEK_*_HOME unquoted, a crafted value executes on the next sync. Undemonstrated: no lane traced a request-supplied value into the writer.
